evidence_warning: Scenario 1-7 objects and allowlisted v3.3 evidence are reused unchanged. The Scenario 8 entry inside runtime_checks_v33.json is historical and noncanonical. Scenario 8-13 current results come only from the redacted v3.4 machine ledger and file-backed v3.4 evidence.

scenarios.name: Account A authenticated state

steps.action: Health-check API and preview and log in as Account A through local OTP UI.
Check home, profile, settings, favorites, meal plan and shopping list.
Require Account A private state and reject Account B private relationships/state.
Classify shared recipe overlap separately from private ownership.

scenarios.expected_result: All six Account A surfaces contain only Account A private state; shared public recipe content is allowed.
scenarios.actual_result: All six surfaces passed private-state isolation. The Account B fixture recipe title appeared only as public shared content; no Account B favorite relation, profile, setting, plan, shopping item, private explanation or account scope appeared.
scenarios.notes: No redirect, indefinite loading, visible runtime error or horizontal overflow. Shopping-list verification is recorded in the redacted runtime ledger; no screenshot was successfully captured for that route.

scenarios.name: Account B fixture verification

steps.action: Log in as Account B through local OTP UI.
Check the same six private surfaces.
Verify Account B private state and absence of Account A private relationships/state.

scenarios.expected_result: Account B private markers differ from Account A and no Account A private state is visible.
scenarios.actual_result: Six of six surfaces passed. B profile, settings, favorite, Friday plan slot and shopping item were present; A private state was absent.
scenarios.notes: The same public recipe catalogue remained allowed. No redirect, visible error or overflow occurred.

scenarios.name: Two-tab Account A

steps.action: Open two controlled tabs under Account A.
Navigate private settings and plan surfaces independently.
Verify both tabs remain Account A scoped with Account B private state absent.

scenarios.expected_result: Both tabs remain correctly scoped to Account A.
scenarios.actual_result: Both tabs shared the same masked session scope and rendered only Account A private state.
scenarios.notes: No raw session or account identifier is recorded.

scenarios.name: Cross-tab logout

steps.action: Log out Account A in the first tab.
Verify both tabs move to login and protected navigation fails closed.
Verify zero private queries/DOM and classify one remaining public catalogue query.

scenarios.expected_result: Logout removes Account A private DOM, protected access and private QueryClient state across tabs.
scenarios.actual_result: Both tabs redirected to login. Private query and DOM counts were zero. One account-unscoped public recipe-catalogue query remained and was correctly classified as public.
scenarios.notes: The earlier aggregate zero-query oracle was corrected to zero private queries.

scenarios.name: Account A to logout to Account B without restart

steps.action: Continue after Account A logout without restarting the Chrome profile.
Log in as Account B through local OTP UI.
Verify B profile, favorite, plan and shopping private state and zero A private state.

scenarios.expected_result: Account B surfaces contain no Account A private marker after a same-profile switch.
scenarios.actual_result: All four required private surfaces showed only Account B state; Account A private markers were absent.
scenarios.notes: A screenshot attempt timed out and is not claimed as evidence.

scenarios.name: Back and forward after account switch

steps.action: Traverse ten history entries backward after the B login.
Traverse ten entries forward.
Check route-specific private ownership after every transition.

scenarios.expected_result: History cannot restore Account A private DOM or query state.
scenarios.actual_result: Twenty history transitions completed with zero Account A private restoration, visible runtime errors or horizontal overflow.
scenarios.notes: Checks used route-specific private markers so public recipe titles could not create a false positive.

scenarios.name: Offline or network failure

steps.action: Open an authenticated Account B private route.
Apply Chrome offline network conditions and reload.
Verify no private A or B DOM is served and restore online health.

scenarios.expected_result: Offline private access fails closed and online health recovers.
scenarios.actual_result: The offline reload produced Chrome's network-failure page with no private DOM. Online recovery returned the Account B profile and no Account A state.

scenarios.name: Legacy service-worker migration

steps.action: Create and confirm one disposable legacy private cache in an isolated persistent profile.
Activate the current generated service worker under system Chrome controlled by Playwright.
Read post-activation Cache Storage and compare it with the exact public allowlist.
Verify legacy-cache count, private API cache count and disallowed request count are zero.

scenarios.expected_result: The current worker deletes legacy private caches and leaves only allowlisted public caches.
scenarios.actual_result: The legacy cache was present before activation and absent afterward. The final cache oracle observed one exact 12-request precache, one approved public runtime cache, zero API-origin entries, zero non-GET requests, zero legacy names and zero disallowed names or requests.
scenarios.notes: Playwright 1.61.1 used system Chrome and a disposable persistent profile. The Chrome extension was not used.

scenarios.name: Consent grant

steps.action: Grant analytics and personalization independently under the current policy.
Read canonical decisions through the authenticated API and database.
Generate one qualifying optional event inside the active grant epoch.

scenarios.expected_result: Separate current-policy grants permit one controlled optional event.
scenarios.actual_result: Both purposes were independently canonical, API and DB readback passed, two consent-ledger rows were observed and exactly one expected optional event was present within the analytics grant epoch.
scenarios.notes: Only masked scope and canonical purpose metadata are retained.

scenarios.name: In-flight withdrawal plus event plus refresh

steps.action: Hold the user-row transaction boundary with zero baseline waiter.
Start withdrawal, then a qualifying optional event, and prove two distinct lock waiters.
Refresh while both operations remain pending and prove the same waiters remain blocked.
Release the barrier and read canonical consent plus post-epoch residue.

scenarios.expected_result: A genuine concurrent race resolves to the canonical epoch with zero post-withdrawal residue.
scenarios.actual_result: Baseline waiter count was zero, withdrawal produced one waiter, the overlapping event produced a second distinct waiter, both remained blocked across refresh, and the barrier was released after 98 ms. Canonical analytics state was withdrawn; dropped event and outbox residue were zero; all audited optional rows after the withdrawal epoch were zero.
scenarios.notes: The proof is lock-waiter based; no sequential substitute is claimed.

scenarios.name: Re-consent without replay

steps.action: Grant analytics again after the committed withdrawal.
Wait without a new qualifying action and compare optional-row counts.
Generate one explicit post-grant action and verify only that new action is accepted.

scenarios.expected_result: Re-consent does not replay a previously dropped event.
scenarios.actual_result: The optional-row count remained unchanged without a new action, replayed-row count was zero, and exactly one explicit post-grant action produced one new row.

scenarios.name: Delayed response during account switch

steps.action: Hold one private Account A favorites response and prove its query is pending.
Log out Account A and log in Account B without restarting the browser profile.
Establish a fresh Account B query, then release the delayed Account A response.
Verify the Account A query never joins Account B QueryClient state or private DOM.

scenarios.expected_result: A delayed Account A response cannot populate Account B UI or QueryClient state.
scenarios.actual_result: The held response contained the expected Account A marker, but its query membership was absent after logout, before release under B and after release. The fresh Account B response used the B authorization scope, contained B state, excluded A state and remained unchanged after release.
scenarios.notes: No raw response body, credential or account identifier is retained.

scenarios.name: Direct masked QueryClient inspection

steps.action: Inspect masked QueryClient metadata while Account A is active.
Inspect after Account A logout and require zero rows.
Inspect Account B active state and after delayed Account A release.
Classify account-neutral public recipe queries separately from private scope.

scenarios.expected_result: Masked inspection shows no Account A private scope after logout or Account B login.
scenarios.actual_result: Masked Account A rows were present only before logout. The after-logout checkpoint had zero rows. Account B had a distinct current scope before and after delayed release, with no Account A query membership; the public recipes namespace remained separately classified as account-neutral.
scenarios.notes: Only namespace, query-key hash, masked scope, status and data-present metadata are retained.
